tagline.text: A private beach resort on Bataan's southern tip, reached by ferry from Manila

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,000~3,000 (per person for a ferry day trip)

children.text: A private beach resort of several hundred hectares at the southwestern end of the Bataan Peninsula in Mariveles. It can be reached by ferry from the CCP Complex in Manila, and its water park and infinity pool make it a popular family day trip.

Camaya Coast is a beach resort and residential development in Sitio Wain, Barangay Biaan, Mariveles, at the southwestern end of the Bataan Peninsula. Sources differ on the total area, with Wikipedia giving 450 hectares and a company profile 354 hectares, so it is generally said to be about 350 to 450 hectares. The coastline is about 3.2 km with two small coves (the white sand beach itself is about 1 km). The developer is Earth and Shore Leisure Communities, and about 30% of the land is said to be left as natural forest. It has become an easy weekend escape for people from Manila, and Filipino-Korean families often mention it as a place to bring children.

The most important point first: this is not a public beach that anyone can walk into, but a private resort with controlled entry. Day guests also need to book in advance, and reviews say walk-ins are either not accepted or must pay a much higher rate. Once your dates are set, book first on the official site (camayacoast.com) or on Klook. A ticket generally includes the beach, the infinity pool and Aqua Fun Water Park.
The sea itself is not a Boracay-style white-sand beach with clear coral water

. The sand is dark gray, and the water is clear but dark, with almost no coral or fish, so it is not suited to snorkeling or freediving. Instead, it is a sheltered cove with a gentle slope and calm waves, which is good for children and weak swimmers, and there are lifeguards and a first-aid station. Think of it as a trip for resort-style fun such as the water park, pools, kayaks, bicycles, weekend band shows and fireworks rather than for the sea itself, and your expectations will match what you find.
Getting there is part of the fun. A boat from the dedicated ferry terminal near the CCP Complex in Manila reaches the resort pier in about
1.5–2 hours
. By road it takes about
3.5–4 hours

even in good traffic, and public transport is poor, so for travelers without a car the ferry package is practically the most realistic option. However, ferry times, fares and the terminal location have changed even recently, so be sure to check the official announcement before you leave.
This is the resort's biggest attraction. It has several slides and pools, a falling-coconut play feature, a tandem slide for two, and a rooftop deck bar. Going first, around
before the crowds build, helps you cut the queues.

blocks.title: Shallow beach in a sheltered cove

children.text: The gentle slope and calm water suit children and beginner swimmers. Swimming is usually allowed until
, lifeguards are on duty, and you should stay inside the areas marked by buoys. The sand is grayish and there is almost no coral.

Climb the stairs on the left side of the beach to reach a multi-level infinity pool. You can soak in warm water while looking down at the sea, though some visitors say that trees and pavilion roofs weaken the effect of the pool merging with the horizon.
Many activities are included in the ticket. Kayaks are booked in
30 minutes
slots at the Sports & Recreation booth, and you can also borrow bicycles and gear for volleyball, frisbee and badminton. Availability changes daily, so go to the booth as soon as you arrive.

A free shuttle runs from the floating pier where the ferry docks to the resort center and the water park. The property is large and hard to cover on foot, but the shuttle makes getting around easy even with children.

On Saturday and Sunday evenings, a band, prize games, fire dancers and fireworks are reported. Ferry day guests may find them hard to see because of the return boat, so they suit an overnight stay better.

blocks.title: One night at Aqua Fun Hotel

children.text: Right next to the water park is a hotel with 49 themed rooms. Rooms have sea, mountain or water park views, and staying over gives you the evening scenery and a relaxed morning on the beach that a day trip lacks.

items.title: Ferry day trip
items.subtitle: A round trip on the morning boat from Manila

children.text: Arrive at the terminal and check in with your booking QR code and a government-issued ID. Arriving about
1.5 hours
before departure is recommended; check-in closes
30 minutes
before departure and the boarding gate closes
15 minutes
before.
The morning ferry departs. Resort meals are on the pricey side, so it helps to eat breakfast before boarding.
Step off at the floating pier and take the shuttle, then book your kayak and inflatable playground times first at the Sports & Recreation booth. Rent a locker now as well.
Head to Aqua Fun Water Park first. The trick is to ride the slides before the midday queues get long.
Have lunch at a resort restaurant and rest in a shaded spot or by the pool. There is little shade at midday and it is hot.
Enjoy beach swimming, kayaking and sand play. If a jellyfish warning is posted, follow the instructions.
Finish showering and packing, then head to the pier.
The return ferry leaves the resort.
The ferry time on your booking confirmation is the one that counts. If you miss it, the booking may be forfeited, so be sure to check.

items.title: Two days, one night
items.subtitle: Stay at the hotel and enjoy the evening show

children.text: Arrive by ferry or car, leave your bags at the hotel and spend your time at the water park and pools. Hotel check-in is at
After check-in, enjoy a beach walk, kayaking and bicycles.
On weekends, watch the band, fire dancers and fireworks. Restaurants get crowded at mealtimes, so it is better to eat early or late.
Check-out is at
. Before then, walk the quiet morning beach and have breakfast.
If you have your own car, you can also stop at one or two Bataan sights such as Mount Samat on the way back.
The one-night rate and the weekend event schedule vary by season, so check before booking.

The ferry departs from the Camaya Coast Manila Ferry Terminal near PICC in the CCP Complex. It moved in November 2024 from the Esplanade terminal next to SM Mall of Asia, so do not follow older articles.
The crossing takes about
1.5–2 hours
. The first morning boat leaves around
, and the return boat is reported to leave the resort at
Check-in closes
30 minutes
before departure and the gate closes
15 minutes
before. You need the booking QR code and a government-issued ID, hand luggage is limited to
7 kg
per person and is inspected. Pregnant women are reportedly restricted from boarding.

To reach the terminal, take the EDSA Carousel to Roxas Boulevard Station, then a jeepney and walk, or take LRT-1 to Vito Cruz station, then a bus or UV Express toward PITX, get off at Diosdado Macapagal Boulevard and walk.
Take NLEX toward SCTEX, leave at the Dinalupihan exit, pass along the Roman Superhighway and enter the Bagac–Mariveles Road. The trip takes about
3.5–4 hours
From Mariveles town to the resort is about
25–40 minutes
by car. Even in traffic, this stretch has many downhill sections and curves, so drive slowly.
Round-trip tolls and fuel are reported at about ₱2,500~3,000. Registered day and overnight guests can use free parking.
It is hard to get there by public transport alone. Some packages reportedly run a shuttle bus from the FAB Central Terminal in Mariveles, so check when booking.
International travelers can land at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) and take a taxi or Grab to the ferry terminal in the CCP Complex, which is the simplest option.
Bataan has no commercial airport, and the nearest international airport is Manila.

The best months to enjoy the resort are November to May, the amihan season. Within that, December to February is relatively cool and the most comfortable. March to May is peak season with strong sun and the biggest crowds, and Holy Week is especially busy.
June to October is the habagat rainy season, with heavy rain and typhoons that can cancel ferries suddenly. Before you go, check the PAGASA forecast and ask the resort whether the ferry is running.

items.note: Room only, breakfast not included, Deluxe at the low end and suites at the high end

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Aqua Fun Hotel is the main place to stay. It is a themed hotel with 49 rooms next to the water park, and Deluxe Queen and Twin rooms are reported at about
and Executive and Family Suites at about
. All are room-only rates without breakfast and can change without notice. Check-in is at
and check-out is at
. It works well to arrive early, leave your bags and start playing.

Restaurants include familiar Philippine brands such as Pancake House, Teriyaki Boy, Dencio's, Tapa King, Figaro, Yellow Cab, Nacho King, Potato Corner and Big Chill. Prices are a little higher than at city branches, and service is slow at mealtimes.
Outside food and drinks are restricted
and bags are inspected, but light snacks and water are reportedly allowed. There are water refill stations, so bringing your own bottle helps.
Book ahead on the official site or Klook. Weekdays are much cheaper and promos change often, so compare prices for your own dates.
When you arrive, go to the Sports & Recreation booth first and reserve your kayak, bicycle and inflatable playground times. Weekends fill up quickly.
A ferry day trip makes for a fairly tight day. Eating breakfast beforehand can save you money on resort food.
Pack reef-safe sunscreen (without oxybenzone, benzophenone or parabens), a hat, sunglasses and a rash guard. There is little shade from 10:00 to 15:00.
Cards are mostly accepted, but some kiosks may not take reloadable cards and there is a locker deposit, so bring ₱500~1,000 in cash separately.
Some water park slides do not allow action cameras, jewelry, sunglasses or loose items. Put valuables in a dry bag and leave them in a locker.
Prepare an extra towel, a change of clothes, slippers and a water bottle. It is better for your skin to change out of wet swimwear right away.
Many reviews say the Wi-Fi is slow. Download any information you need for the trip in advance.
It is hard to enter without a booking at a private resort, the ferry cannot be boarded once the gate closes, and at some point tickets are non-refundable.
Swimming may be banned when a jellyfish warning is issued, and jellyfish have been reported near the floating pier at low tide. Check conditions as soon as you arrive.
Sea lice may appear from March to June, so shower right after leaving the water and change out of wet clothes.
The floating pier can sway and be slippery at low tide, so hold the railing and do not let go of a child's hand.
Children must be watched by a guardian at all times. Do not go beyond the buoy-marked zones and kayak zones, and do not run or climb near railings.
In the rainy season, typhoons and high waves can change ferry operations. Check the announcements the day before and on the morning of departure.
A Pacific War memorial in central Bataan. The overland travel distance should be checked locally, but it is a good stop on the way back.
A heritage village of relocated and restored Spanish-era houses on the Bagac coast, which pairs well with an overnight stay.
The provincial capital of Bataan, convenient for shopping and meals, reached by car.
A marine leisure area on the opposite western coast of the Bataan Peninsula, which you can plan together when you have a longer car itinerary.
